## Frequently Asked Questions

What is GLM-Legal?

GLM-Legal is a legal-domain AI model from Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI), announced on 12 October 2026. It is built on GLM-5.3-Flash and trained further on legal text and simulated legal tasks, so it can review contracts, analyze evidence and plan compliance work. It is in a gated beta, so you apply for API access rather than signing up.

How good is GLM-Legal on legal benchmarks?

Vals AI measured 19.17% on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, 7th of 79 models, and 86.23% on LegalBench, 14th of 150. That puts GLM-Legal level with Gemini 4 Argon on Harvey's test, but behind Meta's Muse Spark models, which Z.ai's own launch chart leaves out.

How much does GLM-Legal cost? [...] | What Z.ai says or shows |

| Base model | GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 18B active |
| Context window | 1M tokens; 128k max output (Vals model card) |
| Input | Text only in Vals testing, even though the base model handles images |
| Target work | Contract review, evidence analysis, compliance research |
| Target users | Law firms, legal tech companies, in-house teams, solo practitioners |
| Access | API trial by application; AutoClaw support "soon" |
| Price | Not published |
| Weights | No download on Z.ai's Hugging Face page as of 14 October | [...] Is GLM-Legal better than Harvey AI?

They are different things. GLM-Legal is a model you call through an API; Harvey AI is a legal product with workflows, permissions and a firm-wide rollout around models. Harvey also wrote the benchmark GLM-Legal is scored on. For the product comparison, see my Harvey AI alternatives roundup.

Can GLM-Legal replace a lawyer?

No. Even the best model on Harvey's test fully completes about 1 in 4 legal tasks, and GLM-Legal completes about 1 in 5. Z.ai's own demos end in tracked changes for a lawyer to review. Treat it like a fast first-pass associate, and read our notes on AI hallucinations before trusting any citation.
